text: {"facts":[{"statement":"The graph starts with n isolated vertices, and operations add/remove copies of undirected edges or query a vertex’s component size.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"Edge multiplicity matters: a connection remains while at least one copy exists, and removing an absent edge does nothing.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"Constraints are 1 ≤ n,q ≤ 100000, with vertices labeled 1 through n.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"The public examples specify the expected behavior for isolated vertices, parallel edges, self-loops, and changing connectivity.","source_ids":["public1","public2","public3","public4"]}],"open_requirements":["Produce a complete Python 3.11 standard-library program that reads the specified input from stdin and writes one component size per query to stdout.","Support dynamic connectivity under both edge insertions and removals within the stated constraints."],"tentative_options":[{"id":"offline_dynamic_connectivity","method":"Track edge multiplicity over time, convert intervals where an edge is present into segment-tree-over-time events, and use a rollback disjoint-set union structure during traversal.","unverified_assumptions":["A rollback DSU traversal over edge-active intervals fits the time and memory limits at q ≤ 100000."]},{"id":"rebuild_by_blocks","method":"Process operations in blocks, treating edges present throughout a block as a base DSU and handling changes within each block separately.","unverified_assumptions":["A suitable block size and per-block query strategy can meet the limits for these constraints."]}],"possible_checks":["Test cases with self-loops and parallel copies, including removal of only one copy.","Test removals of edges that are absent and verify they have no effect.","Compare component-size answers with the public examples, especially after connectivity splits."]}
